devices.name: Logitech G / Saitek X56 Rhino Stick

identify.note: Separate USB device from the throttle. 046D = Logitech-branded, 0738 = Mad Catz/Saitek-branded. PIDs from community device lists; numbering from the Logitech default-config table. H1 (top-right) = buttons 7-10, H2 (bottom-right) = 11-14 (U,R,D,L); M1/M2/S1 mode switch = 15-17; silver POV hat is POV1 and also buttons 18-21. Confirmed by EDCD EliteCustomButtonNames SaitekX56Joystick map.

devices.name: Logitech G / Saitek X56 Rhino Throttle

identify.note: Separate USB device from the stick. Axes: left lever X, right lever Y, top knob Z, mini-stick Rx/Ry, bottom knob Rz, side rotaries Slider1/Slider2. Buttons 34-36 are the M1/M2/S1 mode knob. H3 = upper thumb hat (20-23), H4 = lower thumb hat (24-27) per EDCD map. Note: the Logitech sheet lists axis X = left lever, Y = right lever whereas the EDCD map names X = Throttle R, Y = Throttle L; verify on hardware.

devices.name: Saitek X52 Flight Control System

identify.note: One USB device with stick + throttle. Numbering assembled from the X52 Pro driver map (0-based there, converted to 1-based DirectInput) and community maps; positions of A/B/C/D/E and the throttle-hat directions should be verified on hardware. Scroll-wheel click, MFD buttons and mouse axes not mapped.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech X52 Pro Flight Control System

names: Saitek X52 Pro Flight Control System
identify.note: One USB device with stick + throttle. Numbering assembled from the X52 Pro driver map (0-based there, converted to 1-based DirectInput) and community maps; positions of A/B/C/D/E and the throttle-hat directions should be verified on hardware. Scroll-wheel click, MFD buttons and mouse axes not mapped.

devices.name: Saitek X55 Rhino Stick

identify.note: Separate USB device. Numbering from the EDRefCard X55 map and template picture: 1 trigger, 2 A (red, top), 3 B (side), 4 C (front), 5 D (pinky button), 6 pinky lever, 7-10 H1, 11-14 H2 (castle hat), POV1 = POV hat; axes X/Y roll/pitch, RZ twist (Logitech support article). The trigger is single-stage (review) and there is no fire button besides A, so trigger stage 2 and the "Fire (red)" entry have no input.

devices.name: Saitek X55 Rhino Throttle

identify.note: Separate USB device. Left lever X, right lever Y (Logitech support article). Rest from the EDRefCard X55 map: F rotary Z, G rotary RX, RTY1 RZ, RTY2 RY, mouse mini-stick U/V (sliders); buttons 1 E, 2 F press, 3 G press, 4 H, 5 I, 6-11 SW1-SW6, 12-19 TGL1-TGL4 up/down, 20-23 H3, 24-27 H4, 28/29 pinky rocker, 30/31 pinky spin wheel. No source gives a number for the mini-stick press or for the two slider entries.

devices.name: Saitek X65F Pro Flight System

identify.note: Force-sensing (non-moving) stick with throttle; VID:PID not found. Discontinued.

devices.name: Saitek X45 Digital Flight Control System

identify.note: Stick + throttle on one USB id (discontinued). Buttons from the EDRefCard and FlightGear X45 maps (they agree): 1 trigger, 2 A, 3 B, 4 launch, 5 throttle D, 6 throttle mouse button, 7 pinkie, 8 C, 15-18 upper stick hat, 19-22 throttle forefinger hat, 23-26 throttle thumb hat; lower stick hat = POV1. 9-14 are the mode/aux switch positions (the two maps describe them differently, so not listed). Throttle axis: EDRefCard says U (slider), FlightGear says Windows axis 2 - not set. Doubt: the X45 stick has no twist; RZ is the rudder rocker on the throttle (EDRefCard), so the stick.axis.twist entry is really that rocker.

devices.name: Saitek X36 / X36F Flight Control System

identify.note: Stick + throttle (discontinued). Button numbering not verified.

devices.name: Saitek Cyborg / Evo joysticks (Cyborg 3D, Evo, Evo Force)

identify.note: Family entry: several models with different button counts. Evo ids per devicehunt: 0464 and 35BE Cyborg Evo, FFB5 Evo Force, 353E Evo Wireless. Trigger = button 1 per the FlightGear Cyborg Evo map; other numbers differ per model.

devices.name: Logitech Extreme 3D Pro

identify.note: 12 buttons, one 8-way hat, X/Y/twist + throttle slider. Buttons 1-2 trigger/side thumb, 3-6 top of the stick, 7-12 base (ordering inside groups not verified against a published map).

devices.name: Logitech Attack 3

identify.note: 11 buttons, 8-way hat, throttle slider, no twist. VID:PID unverified; numbering not verified.

devices.name: Logitech Freedom 2.4 Cordless Joystick

identify.note: Discontinued wireless stick; VID:PID not found, numbering not verified.

devices.name: Logitech G940 Flight System (force feedback)

identify.note: FFB stick + throttle (+pedals); discontinued. Joystick, throttle and pedals are separate USB devices on Windows (EDRefCard: LogitechG940Joystick/Throttle/Pedals); this entry is the joystick. Joystick buttons per EDRefCard and FlightGear (agree): 1 trigger first stage, 9 second stage, 2 FIRE, 3-7 S1-S5, 8 mini-stick press, POV1 hat; mini-stick X = V (slider 2), Y = U (slider 1). Doubt: EDRefCard lists RX/RY/RZ as the TRIM 2/3/1 wheels, which contradicts the existing stick.axis.twist = JOY_RZ (the G940 stick has no twist). Throttle axes are on the separate throttle device and have no numbers here. Elite Dangerous DeviceMappings: G940 Joystick 046D:C2A8, Throttle 046D:C2A9, Pedals 046D:C2AA (the throttle and pedal ids are separate devices and not matched by this entry); the older id C287 is unverified.

devices.name: Saitek Pro Flight Rudder Pedals

identify.note: Rudder + two toe brakes. X = left toe brake, Y = right toe brake, RZ = rudder (EDRefCard map; FlightGear map: axes 0/1 = left/right brake, rudder = Windows axis 3).

devices.name: Saitek Pro Flight Combat Rudder Pedals

names: Saitek Pro Flight Combat Rudder Pedals
identify.note: Rudder + two toe brakes. X = left toe brake, Y = right toe brake, RZ = rudder per FlightGear map; EDRefCard gives the same layout but marks the toe brakes unconfirmed.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Yoke

identify.note: Per Logitech user guide: T1..T6 = buttons 3..8 (three 2-way rockers; which side is up/down is not documented, so mapped as plain buttons). Mode switch (3-pos) has no documented numbers. 712C = integrated USB hub. The quadrant that ships with the yoke system plugs into the yoke and then reports on the yoke device: levers Z, Rx, Ry and T1-T6 = buttons 15-20 (Logitech yoke system manual); lever detent buttons have no documented numbers there.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Throttle Quadrant

identify.note: Standalone USB device (06A3:0C2D): levers left to right = X, Y, Z; rockers T1-T6 = buttons 1-6; lever pulled below the detent = buttons 7 (left), 8 (middle), 9 (right) per FlightGear map and an MSFS forum report (button 8 = middle lever full back). CHANGED: earlier this entry used Z/Rx/Ry and buttons 15-20; that is the Logitech manual numbering for the quadrant plugged into the Pro Flight Yoke, now listed on the yoke entry.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Switch Panel

identify.note: 13 toggle switches + magneto key (OFF/R/L/BOTH/START) + gear lever. Numbering is the commonly used left-to-right order from community maps, not a manufacturer table; each toggle reports one held button when ON (only the ON position is listed). Doubt: forum sources say the Saitek switch/radio/multi panels are not seen as DirectInput game controllers (they need SPAD.neXt or plug-ins); the button numbers here only apply where a tool exposes them as buttons.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Radio Panel

identify.note: Two LCD rows, two selector knobs (COM1/COM2/NAV1/NAV2/ADF/DME/XPDR), two dual encoders, ACT/STBY buttons. Button numbers not verified. Not a DirectInput game controller: Windows and games do not list it as a joystick; it needs SPAD.neXt, the Saitek/Logitech plug-ins or a sim with native support, so no JOY_ inputs exist.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Multi Panel

identify.note: Autopilot panel: selector ALT/VS/IAS/HDG/CRS, rotary encoder, AP/HDG/NAV/IAS/ALT/VS/APR/REV buttons, A/T, flaps lever, pitch-trim wheel. Button numbers not verified. Not a DirectInput game controller: Windows and games do not list it as a joystick; it needs SPAD.neXt, the Saitek/Logitech plug-ins or a sim with native support, so no JOY_ inputs exist.

devices.name: Saitek Pro Flight Instrument Panel

identify.note: Mainly an output/display panel (gauge LCDs driven by plugin); few or no inputs. Not verified.

devices.name: Saitek Pro Flight Backlit Information Panel (BIP)

names: Saitek Pro Flight Backlit Information Panel
identify.note: Output-only annunciator panel (backlit indicator lights); no DirectInput inputs.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech Farm Sim Side Panel Control Deck

identify.note: Mainly a farming control deck, also used as a generic panel in X-Plane; only marginally flight-relevant; numbering not verified.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Cessna Rudder Pedals

Mad Catz Pro Flight Cessna Rudder Pedals
identify.note: Cessna-styled version of the Pro Flight Rudder Pedals; same axis layout (X left toe brake, Y right toe brake, RZ rudder) per EDRefCard and the FlightGear pedal map that lists this name.

devices.name: Saitek / Logitech G Pro Flight Cessna Trim Wheel

names: Saitek Pro Flight Cessna Trim Wheel
Mad Catz Pro Flight Cessna Trim Wheel
identify.note: Single-axis elevator trim wheel (axis 0 = X per FlightGear map). One FSUIPC forum user reported PID 0C2D, which is the Throttle Quadrant id; 0BD4 is the id in the driver database and other logs.

devices.name: Saitek Pro Flight Cessna Yoke (with built-in throttle / prop / mixture levers)

names: Mad Catz Pro Flight Cessna Yoke
identify.note: Discontinued. Button numbers from the FlightGear map (0-based there, +1 here). The three levers (throttle black, prop blue, mixture red) and the coolie hat are given there only as Windows multimedia axis indices, so no DirectInput axis names are set for them.

devices.name: Saitek / Mad Catz Pro Flight TPM System (Throttle, Prop, Mixture)

names: Mad Catz Pro Flight TPM System
identify.note: VID:PID, device name and axes from the vendor driver INF (Pro_Flight_TPM_System_7_0_47_1 on download01.logi.com, Sai0B4D.inf): OEM axis 0 'Throttle' (X), 1 'Prop' (Y), 5 'Mixture' (Rz). Nine toggle switches (Saitek product text); a flight-sim blog reports them as buttons with FSX index 0-8 that only fire on the downward action, i.e. JOY_BTN1-9 = switch 1-9 down (left to right not verified). The up position sends nothing. Discontinued; no official photo left on a Logitech host.

devices.name: Saitek Cyborg X / Cyborg F.L.Y.5 / Mad Catz F.L.Y.5 Flight Stick

names: Mad Catz Mad Catz F.L.Y.5 Stick
identify.note: Same stick under three names: the vendor driver INFs (Saitek_Cyborg_X_SD6 and MadCatz_FLY5_SD7_0_24_0 on download01.logi.com) register 06A3:0836 as 'Saitek Cyborg X' and 'Cyborg F.L.Y.5 Flight Stick' and 0738:1302 as 'Mad Catz F.L.Y.5 Flight Stick'. Axes and buttons from the EDRefCard SaitekFLY5 map (Elite Dangerous DeviceMappings lists 0738:1302 as SaitekFLY5): X/Y stick, Rz twist, Z throttle, POV1 hat; labels are EDRefCard's descriptions (exact physical spots of buttons 10-14 not verified).

devices.name: Saitek Aviator / A.V.8.R. Stick (AV8R-01, AV8R-02, AV8R-03, Mad Catz Pacific A.V.8.R.)

identify.note: Vendor driver INFs on download01.logi.com: 06A3:0461 'Saitek Aviator Stick' (Saitek_Aviator_SD6) and 0738:4213 'Mad Catz Pacific Aviator Stick' (Pacific Aviator SD7), both with OEM axes X, Y, 'Throttle 1' = Z, 'Throttle 2' = slider 1, 'Twist' = Rz. 06A3:0C28 is Elite Dangerous' SaitekAV8R03 (alternative 0461); 0738:CB29 is 'Saitek Aviator Stick AV8R02' in usb.ids (same layout assumed, not verified). Buttons per the FlightGear Aviator map (numbers identical on Windows): 1 trigger, 2 left, 3 center, 4 right head button, 5-12 base switches T1-T8 (each flip switch sends two of them; which one is up is not documented, so listed as plain buttons), 13/14 mode switch positions 1/2.

devices.name: Saitek ST290 Pro Flight Stick

identify.note: All four ids are registered as 'Saitek ST290 Pro' by the vendor driver INF (Saitek_ST290Pro_SD6 on download01.logi.com); Elite Dangerous DeviceMappings uses 0460. Buttons per the FlightGear ST290-Pro map: button n = the printed number n (1 = trigger); positions of 2-6 on the stick not verified. Throttle and twist DirectInput axes are not documented (FlightGear: Windows axis 2 throttle, 3 twist) - left without input; hat = POV.

devices.name: Saitek ST290 Stick

identify.note: VID:PID and name from the vendor driver INF (Saitek_ST290_SD6 on download01.logi.com) and usb.ids. Predecessor of the ST290 Pro; control list only, numbering not documented.

devices.name: Saitek / Mad Catz Cyborg V.1 Stick

identify.note: 06A3:0D25 'Saitek Cyborg V.1 Stick' from the vendor driver INF (Saitek_Cyborg_V1_Stick_SD6_8_0_6 on download01.logi.com); 0738:2237 'V.1 Stick' from usb.ids (Mad Catz id, not verified as the same model). Ambidextrous stick with trigger, five buttons, pinky shift button, POV hat, throttle lever and twist (retailer descriptions); numbering not documented.

devices.name: Saitek Cyborg 3D Gold USB Stick

identify.note: Names and button names/numbers from the FlightGear Cyborg-Gold-3d-USB map: 1 trigger, 2-4 left/middle/right head buttons, 5-8 F1-F4, 9 '>>', 10 '<<', the hat as buttons 11 up, 12 left, 13 right, 14 down. VID:PID 06A3:0006 'Cyborg Gold Joystick' per usb.ids (assumed to be this stick). Rudder (twist) and throttle DirectInput axes not documented. Base positions of F1-F4 and the shift buttons not verified.

devices.name: Logitech G940 Flight System - Throttle

identify.note: Separate USB device of the G940 system (Elite Dangerous DeviceMappings: LogitechG940Throttle 046D:C2A9; the joystick is logitech-g940, the pedals logitech-g940-pedals). Split dual throttle, two rotary controls R1/R2, two hat switches (Logitech: eight-way), four grip buttons T1-T4, eight base buttons P1-P8 with LEDs and a 3-position mode switch (Logitech press release, Linux kernel patch). DirectInput numbering not documented.

devices.name: Logitech G940 Flight System - Rudder Pedals

identify.note: Separate USB device of the G940 system (Elite Dangerous DeviceMappings: LogitechG940Pedals 046D:C2AA). Rudder = Rz per the EDRefCard G940 pedals map; EDRefCard puts the toe brakes on X (right) and Y (left) but marks both unconfirmed, so they have no input here.

devices.name: Logitech Force 3D Pro (force feedback)

identify.note: VID:PID 'Force 3D Pro' per usb.ids. FlightGear's force-3d-pro map states its button numbers follow the numbers printed on the stick (button 1 = trigger ... 12); twist and throttle slider exist (FlightGear: Windows axes 3 and 2) but their DirectInput tokens are not documented. Head/base split of 3-12 assumed like the Extreme 3D Pro (same body), not verified.

devices.name: Logitech WingMan Strike Force 3D (force feedback)

FlightGear map: trigger = button 1, second hat H2 = buttons 10 up, 11 right, 12 down, 13 left; first hat = POV. Twist and throttle exist, DirectInput tokens not documented. Other buttons not mapped here.

devices.name: Logitech WingMan Extreme Digital 3D

identify.note: Predecessor of the Extreme 3D Pro: 7 buttons, 8-way hat, twist and throttle slider (FlightGear wingman-extreme-digital-3d map). Both ids are 'WingMan Extreme Digital 3D' in usb.ids. Discontinued; numbering not documented.

devices.name: Logitech WingMan Force 3D (force feedback)

identify.note: Force feedback stick with twist, throttle slider and hat (FlightGear wingman-force-3d map). VID:PID per usb.ids. Discontinued; numbering not documented.

devices.name: Logitech WingMan Force (force feedback, serial/USB)

identify.note: Dual-mode serial/USB force feedback stick with throttle slider and hat (FlightGear wingman-force map). VID:PID per usb.ids. Discontinued; numbering not documented.

devices.name: Logitech WingMan Attack 2

identify.note: Budget stick with throttle; VID:PID per usb.ids. Successor of the gameport WingMan Attack. Discontinued; numbering not documented.

devices.name: Logitech WingMan Extreme (USB, with throttle)

names: Logitech WingMan Extreme Joystick with Throttle
identify.note: 'WingMan Extreme Joystick with Throttle' per usb.ids (046D:0200 'WingMan Extreme Joystick' is probably the throttle-less variant, not listed). Discontinued; numbering not documented.
